body.name: Atomic row-recovery map
body.construction: For \(i\in A\), let \(\tau_h\mu\) denote translation of a probability law \(\mu\) by \(h\). Define \(T_i\) as the unique linear map satisfying \(K_{\{i\}}(x)=\tau_{T_i x}K_{\{i\}}(0)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R\); existence follows from \(\texttt{lem:intervention-pushforward}\) and uniqueness from \(\texttt{lem:probability-translation-rigidity}\). Obtain the unordered projective rows \(\mathscr R_i\) of an ICA unmixing matrix directly from \(K_{\{i\}}(0)\); arbitrary source locations do not change these projective rows. Lift \([v]\in\mathscr R_i\) by \(\Lambda_i(v,T_i)_{X\setminus\{i\}}=v\) and \(\Lambda_i(v,T_i)_i=-vT_i\). Define \(\rho_i(\Pi_A\mathbf K)\) as the unique element of \(\mathscr R(Q)\setminus\{[\Lambda_i(v,T_i)]:[v]\in\mathscr R_i\}\), normalize its representative \(q_i\) by \((q_i)_i=1\), and return \(\operatorname{rec}_i(\Pi_A\mathbf K)=e_i^\top-q_i\).
